lancelot.summary: Jungle assassin built on the sequence of dashes, with a window of invulnerability during the ultimate.
lancelot.analysis:
Lancelot goes through a fight rather than entering it. His skill 2 marks targets, his skill 1 recharges by hitting a marked target: well chained, he can dash almost without interruption as long as he hits something.

His ultimate makes him invulnerable during the animation, which also makes it a defensive tool to dodge a check or an execution. The hero is punished by anything that blocks movement – ​​Khufra in the lead – and by areas that prevent him from moving forward.

builds.name: Standard Jungle
builds.context: The reference build: penetration then a survival item to hold the second rotation.

gusion.summary: Combo magic assassin: he places his daggers, teleports on them, and picks them up to inflict all his damage at once.
gusion.analysis:
Gusion is the most demanding combo hero in the game after Fanny. All of his skills can be rerolled, and the order and timing of the rerolls entirely determine his damage. The standard combo is to put the daggers down, get close with the ultimate, then trigger the recovery so everything happens simultaneously.

A mastered Gusion takes out any fragile target in less than a second, often before the opponent's screen has shown anything. A rough Gusion does a third of the damage and dies on the spot. Few heroes have such a wide gap between the two.
skills: After a skill, his next basic attack deals additional damage proportional to the target's missing health.

ling.summary: Assassin who moves on walls, out of range, and chooses his moment to fall on a target.
ling.analysis:
Ling changes the geometry of the map. While on a wall, he is untouchable by most ground skills, allowing him to wait indefinitely for the opening. It does not use mana but an energy resource, which limits the number of consecutive jumps.

His ultimate makes him immune to checks while leaping and deals critical damage. The hero is excellent in mobile skirmishing and weak against a grouped team that keeps his controls to himself. Khufra remains his clearest response.

builds.name: Critical Jungle
builds.context: His ultimate deals critical damage: critical rate is worth more than raw penetration.

yi-sun-shin.summary: Hybrid jungler who switches from bow to sword depending on the distance, and whose ultimate reveals the entire map.
yi-sun-shin.analysis:
Yi Sun-shin changes weapons on his own: he shoots a bow from afar and strikes with a sword on contact, and each change strengthens his next two attacks. His skill 1 propels him forward by briefly rendering him immune to controls, and his recharge decreases with each successful weapon change. The ultimate first gives him vision of the entire map and an acceleration, then, restarted, sends a ship which stuns the center of the zone before a barrage which slows down: it is as much an information tool as a remote initiation.

His measured performance is concentrated at the start of the game: his victory rate is significantly higher in games finished before the twelfth minute, then returns to around the average. He therefore lives from the advance gained in the jungle rather than from the end of the game, and his only protection against controls only lasts an instant. The measurements place him in difficulty against Karina, Uranus, Aamon, Johnson and Hayabusa, from Mythic rank to Mythic Glory rank.

selena.summary: Heroine with two forms: traps and stun arrow from a distance, then assassination on contact after the ultimate.
selena.analysis:
Selena is played in two stages. In her elven form, she places demons that watch over a location and cling to passing enemies, and she shoots an arrow whose stun lengthens with the distance traveled; his skills leave marks on targets. The ultimate switches her to Abyssal Form, where her skills become a leaping attack with shield and a charge, which consume these marks for additional damage; she can then return to elven form.

This versatility has a cost: its entire initiation relies on the arrow, which must start from afar to stun for a long time. His measured win rate remains below average at all ranks, with a low point in games lasting less than twelve minutes. It is played in the middle lane as well as in roam, with different objects depending on the position. The measurements place her in difficulty against Gloo, Popol and Kupa, Chip and Lolita.

chou.summary: Isolation fighter: he extracts a target from the opposing group and kills it before his team reacts.
chou.analysis:
Chou is the highest ceiling hero in roam. The idea is simple – the ultimate sends a target into the air and moves it – but its execution relies on animation cancellations that the game nowhere explains. The reference combo chains skill 1, canceled jump, ultimate, then skill 2 to hold the target upon landing.

His interest in an organized team comes from there: he chooses who dies. Against a player who keeps his Purify, on the other hand, the ultimate loses half of its value, and Chou becomes an average fighter again.

yu-zhong.summary: Experienced lane fighter who heals himself on hitting and becomes very difficult to kill in prolonged combat.
yu-zhong.analysis:
Yu Zhong wins fights that last. Its passive transforms part of the damage inflicted into a shield, which makes it excellent when there are several targets in range - a five-way confrontation gives it much more return than a duel.

His ultimate makes him immune to checks while he advances, which also makes him a credible initiator. Countering it almost always involves reducing healing: without it, a well-equipped Yu Zhong absorbs an entire team.

builds.name: Regeneration experience

paquito.summary: Window Fighter: Each skill used improves the next, for a very short damage peak.
paquito.analysis:
Paquito is not played skill by skill but by sequences. Each spell cast loads an enhanced version of the next one, and the whole point of it is to string together those enhanced versions in the correct order before the window closes.

Well done, it takes out a weak target in two seconds from a considerable distance. Played poorly, he wastes his upgraded versions on minions and has nothing left. He is a rhythm hero, very sensitive to the player's level.

dyrroth.summary: Rage fighter who removes physical armor from his target before striking them, played in experience lane as well as in jungle.
dyrroth.analysis:
Dyrroth builds up rage while fighting; At mid-gauge, his first two skills become a reinforced version, with more range or more damage. Every two basic attacks he hits in a circle around himself and heals himself, and each hero hit shortens his cooldowns. Skill 2 launches it at a target then, recast, removes a large part of its physical armor for a few seconds: it is the opening which makes the rest of its damage effective. The ultimate leaves after a short delay, cannot be interrupted, and slows down everything it passes through.

He lives on his early game rallies: his measured win rate is highest in short games and drops below average after the eighteenth minute. Its numbers also vary depending on the rank, lower in Mythic than in Mythic Glory. The measures place him in difficulty against Masha, Benedetta and Thamuz.

sun.summary: Fighter who multiplies: his doubles strike with him, heal him and eat away at the targets' armor.
sun.analysis:
Sun fights by summoning doubles. His first two skills throw his staff, which leaves a temporary duplicate; the second additionally hides him while he moves with the stick. The ultimate summons a more durable duplicate, closer to its own stats. Each hit from Sun or his doubles reduces the target's physical armor a little, and each hit from a double heals it: the more doubles there are on a target, the faster it melts and the longer it lasts.

His measured profile is that of a late-game hero: victory rate below average in games lasting less than fourteen minutes, then significantly above after the sixteenth. He is also very often banned, especially at Mythic rank. Double the ultimate takes increased damage, and the metrics put Sun in trouble against Aldous, Natan, Alucard, Joy, and Ruby.

guinevere.summary: Magic damage fighter who knocks her targets into the air, then holds them there under her ultimate.
guinevere.analysis:
Guinevere is built around projection. Her skill 2 makes her leap across an area, sending enemies into the air, then can launch herself again for a short teleport that leaves an illusion behind. She inflicts additional damage on targets in the air, and her hits mark enemies: a target with three marks is projected by her ultimate, which launches enemies already there into the air with each hit, while Guinevere remains unaffected by controls.

Everything therefore depends on skill 2: if the jump fails and the marks are missing, the ultimate loses most of its control. His measured numbers are close to average, a little better in short games, and his ban rate has fallen over the last thirty days. The measurements place her in difficulty against Masha, Wanwan, Khufra, Diggie and Fanny.

kagura.summary: Dual-State Mage: Her skills completely change depending on whether she is holding her umbrella or has it down.
kagura.analysis:
Kagura has eight skills in practice for three hits. Each spell has a version with an umbrella and a version without, and knowing what state you are in is the hero's main thing. The signature combo follows the pose of the umbrella, a rappel that crosses and projects, then the ultimate to lock.

She is also one of the rare mages capable of getting out of a bad position on her own, since teleporting to the umbrella serves as an escape. In return, a status error leaves her without mobility in the middle of the opposing team.

pharsa.summary: Artillery Mage: His ultimate strikes across the map, without ever entering combat.
pharsa.analysis:
Pharsa plays on the scope. Her ultimate is a channeled bombardment covering a huge area from long range, allowing her to participate in a fight she can barely see. Well placed, this spell alone can decide a clash around the lord.

His skill 2 gives him a flying form that passes through walls, essential for repositioning after channeling. The weak point is obvious: during the ultimate she is immobile and defenseless, and any assassin who finds her kills her.

cecilion.summary: Stacking Mage: He accumulates blood throughout the game and becomes an area threat that is impossible to ignore at the end of the game.
cecilion.analysis:
Cecilion is a bet on the long term. Each skill launched adds a permanent charge which increases its damage and its maximum mana - a Cecilion which has farmed quietly for fifteen minutes no longer has anything to do with the one at the beginning.

On the other hand, he is extremely fragile before stacking, and his skills have a wide but slow zone. Faced with a team that attacks him early and often, he never reaches his level. He is the typical hero where the result depends on the pace of the game more than the duel.

novaria.summary: Ranged harassment mage, whose ultimate enlarges the silhouette of targets to make his shots easier to place.
novaria.analysis:
Novaria is played from afar. Her skill 1 places a sphere that hurts and slows down around her before exploding; her skill 2 makes a sphere return to her, giving it speed and the ability to pass through walls, then throws it back towards a hero, with damage that increases with the distance traveled. His spheres reveal nearby enemies, and his ultimate enlarges the impact zone of the heroes hit while revealing their surroundings: this is what makes his long shots reliable.

She has no stuns or freezes, only slows. His measured win rate remains below average at all ranks, but increases with game length and rises above fifty percent after the eighteenth minute. The measurements place her clearly in difficulty against Natalia, then against Zilong, Aldous, Ling and Estes.

eudora.summary: Explosion Mage: Each skill electrifies the target and strengthens the next, up to an area stun.
eudora.analysis:
Eudora works in sequence. Each of his skills electrifies targets hit, and the next skill gains an effect against an electrified target: skill 1 creates a chain that accelerates him and can reduce his cooldown by half, skill 2 changes from a single-target stun to an area stun, and the ultimate triggers an additional explosion around each electrified target. The right order turns a skill rotation into elimination and group control.

Without electrification applied, his skills lose their additional effects: a first failed skill breaks the sequence. His measured win rate is higher in short games and drops back to average after eighteen minutes. Patch 2.1.88 places her among the reinforced heroes, without the wiki detailing the modification. The measures place her in difficulty against Atlas, Masha, Barats and Leomord.

zetian.summary: Mage whose ultimate damages and stuns all opposing heroes, wherever they are on the map.
zetian.analysis:
Zetian combines harassment and global presence. Her skill 1 launches a wave that launches another on each hit, up to three, and she can move and cast other skills during this time; his skill 2 installs a spirit that slows, reduces magic defense and can be redirected. His ultimate accelerates his entire team, injures and briefly stuns each enemy hero and reveals their position: it weighs on a fight even launched on the other side of the map. Her passive also protects her, at long intervals, by pushing back and stunning heroes who approach her.

Its measured performance is regular rather than spectacular: victory rate close to average, with no marked difference depending on the duration of the game, and ban rate down slightly over thirty days. His passive's lifesteal only charges when hitting heroes with his first two skills. The measurements place her in difficulty against Valentina, Floryn, Mathilda, Uranus and Gloo.

vexana.summary: Control mage that summons a fighting guardian, much more effective, according to measurements, in short games than in long ones.
vexana.analysis:
Vexana harasses from a distance and controls on impact. His skill 1 is a projectile that stops on the first hero hit, frightens him and pushes him away before exploding on his neighbors; his skill 2 hits an area after a short delay. His ultimate throws enemies into the air as a guardian arrives, who then fights alongside him for several seconds and hits large areas. Its passive curses targets hit, which explode on their allies if they die.

The measurements place it in the average for all ranks, but with a clear slope: high victory rate in short games, below fifty percent beyond the sixteenth minute. Its delayed skill 2 gives the target time to exit the area. She is in difficulty facing Alice, X.Borg, Marcel, Natalia and Benedetta.

nana.summary: Harassment mage that incapacitates a target by transforming it, and survives a fatal blow once.
nana.analysis:
Nana wears down her opponents from afar with a boomerang that hits back and forth. Her skill 2 sends Molina to pursue the closest enemy hero: the one she hits is transformed for a short time, slowed down and weakened against magic damage. The ultimate hits an area three times and stuns enemies hit multiple times in a row. Her passive grants her, once every two and a half minutes, an invulnerable transformation at the moment she should die.

Its measured figures are low: below average victory rate at all ranks, even lower in Mythic Glory, with no real improvement in long games. While transforming her passive, she cannot cast any skills, and Molina chooses her target herself among nearby heroes. The counter gaps remain modest; the clearest place her in difficulty against Gloo, then against Akai and Hylos.

granger.summary: Magazine Shooter: His damage comes from his skills, not his attack speed.
granger.analysis:
Granger is not built like a classic shooter. His passive sets his attack to six bullets, the last of which is critical, which makes attack speed almost useless on him: you buy attack damage and penetration.

This gives it a very early peak of power, exploitable in the jungle from the first object. His fragility remains that of a shooter, aggravated by the absence of any control: poorly positioned, he only has his skill 2 to hope to escape.

beatrix.summary: Shooter with four weapons, each with its own ultimate: she changes role depending on the weapon carried.
beatrix.analysis:
Beatrix is ​​actually four heroes. She carries two weapons at a time among four, and each redefines its range, its rate and its ultimate: a very long range sniper rifle, an explosive shotgun, a rapid rate assault rifle, an area grenade launcher.

The level of play consists of choosing the correct pair before the game, then alternating in combat. This is what makes it both very strong in competition and very punishing in ranked play: a bad pair, or a bad change at the wrong time, and it no longer has any damage at all.

melissa.summary: Defensive Shooter: Her ultimate creates an area that melee enemies cannot pass through.
melissa.analysis:
Melissa solves the classic shooter problem — getting dunked — with a direct response. His ultimate lays down a circle that knocks back melee opponents and greatly reduces their damage inside, allowing him to keep shooting while an assassin exhausts himself trying to get in.

She remains a standard shooter compared to the rest: good power build-up, decent damage, no threat beyond her reach. Against a ranged team that ignores it and punches through the zone, the ultimate loses most of its value.

miya.summary: Pure basic attack shooter: she gains momentum as long as she hits, and her ultimate makes her disappear the moment you aim her.
miya.analysis:
Miya bases everything on basic attack. Its passive stacks attack speed with each shot that hits, skill 1 adds additional arrows that also damage nearby targets, and skill 2 immobilizes an area before slowing down what's around it. Her ultimate removes the negative effects, makes her invisible and brings her out of this state with her passive already at full charge: it is used as much to escape as to return to the exchange at full speed. Its measured win rate increases slightly with the length of the game.

It has no instantaneous movement. Once the ultimate is used, she only has skill 2 left to slow down an attacker, and her pace drops as soon as she stops hitting a target. The countermeasures place her in difficulty against Beatrix, Granger, Gatotkaca, Karina and Belerick, with a gap which is found from the Mythic rank to the Mythic Glory rank.

hanabi.summary: Rebounding damage shooter, which controls don't hit while she's carrying a shield.
hanabi.analysis:
Hanabi inflicts her damage in ricochet: each basic attack or skill that hits sends blades back to neighboring enemies, making her effective in group fights and on waves. Her skill 1 gives her a shield, and as long as a shield protects her, control effects have no effect on her; part of the damage it inflicts also recharges this shield. His ultimate immobilizes the first hero hit before exploding around him.

However, she has no instantaneous movement: if the shield falls, she becomes an easy target to reach again. His measured win rate is highest in short games and declines significantly as they get longer, falling below fifty percent after the eighteenth minute. At the Mythic Glory rank, the measurements place her in difficulty against Lolita, Joy, Beatrix, Wanwan and Ixia.

lesley.summary: Ranged crit shooter, whose measured win rate goes from very low to high depending on the length of the game.
lesley.analysis:
Lesley plays on range and critical strike. If she hasn't taken damage in a few seconds, her passive lengthens her next basic attack and gives her a high critical chance, and any physical penetration she buys turns into critical damage. Skill 1 camouflages her and strengthens her attack, skill 2 pushes enemies in front of her while making her retreat, and the ultimate locks on to an opposing hero to shoot him four bullets in a row.

The price of this profile can be seen in the measurements: its victory rate across all ranks is below average, with a very low point in games lasting less than fourteen minutes, and only exceeds fifty percent from the eighteenth minute. Her passive cuts off as soon as she is hit, and the ultimate's bullets can be intercepted by another enemy hero placed in front of the target. The measurements place her in difficulty against Sun, Gloo, Estes, Tigreal and Mathilda.

estes.summary: The crudest heal in the game: its ultimate regenerates the entire team for several seconds.
estes.analysis:
Estes does nothing but heal, but he does it at a volume that no other support reaches. In a prolonged fight around an objective, his ultimate can negate an entire composition's worth of sustained damage.

This also makes him the most context-dependent hero on the roster. Against a team that buys healing reduction, or has an initiation capable of removing it first, it becomes almost useless. It provides no control, no damage, no mobility: if it doesn't heal, it doesn't exist.

angela.analysis:
Angela plays a second part in parallel with hers. Her ultimate allows her to join any ally anywhere, giving her a shield and stat boost while she's attached — she literally becomes an extension of the chosen player.

Used well, it allows a wielder to dive with a security they never would alone, and it appears on the other side of the map to turn around a skirmish. Used incorrectly, it passes the game attached to the wrong player and does not influence anything.

mathilda.analysis:
Mathilda is the most versatile support in the game today. His skill 2 involves an ally in his movement, which makes it possible to bring a fighter into contact as well as to get a shooter out of a bad position. His ultimate locks a target and serves as a targeted initiation.

She also has real damage, which makes her playable as a secondary assassin when the game goes wrong. Its difficulty lies in reading: each move involves two players at a time, and an error costs two deaths instead of one.

rafaela.summary: Healing and resurrection support, which brings back a fallen ally without waiting for their respawn timer to end.
rafaela.analysis:
Rafaela combines care, speed and control. His skill 2 heals nearby allies, especially the most injured, and gives them speed with a brief immunity to slowdowns; his skill 1 automatically hits the three closest enemies, revealing them and slowing them; his ultimate stuns on a line. Its passive, above all, allows you to resurrect a fallen ally, who reappears at the base: an opposing elimination therefore costs your team less.

Patch 2.1.88 significantly reduced the base recharge of resurrection, while increasing the part that depends on the ally's reappearance time, strengthened skill 1 and lowered the mana cost of its other skills. His measured win rate is now well above average, and his ban rate is increasing over the last thirty days. Its limit is initiation: a single control, to aim in a straight line. The measurements place her in difficulty against Ixia, Odette, Estes, Layla and Silvanna.

floryn.summary: Global Healing Support: Her ultimate heals the entire team, regardless of where they are on the map.
floryn.analysis:
Floryn heals from a distance and without needing to target her allies. His skill 1 targets an enemy, and healing fruits then bounce towards nearby allies; his skill 2 briefly stuns and reveals enemies hit; his ultimate heals the entire team twice, regardless of distance, and instantly boosts shields and regeneration. His lantern improves his statistics and can be shared with an ally, who then receives a bonus for each of his treatments.

Its measured performance depends strongly on the duration of the game: high victory rate in short games, under fifty percent after the eighteenth minute. Patch 2.1.88 reduced the mana cost of his first two skills. Her best duets measured are with Carmilla and Atlas, and the measurements place her clearly in difficulty against Lolita, then against Yin, Ixia, Baxia and Silvanna.

carmilla.summary: Support tank that links enemies together: control or damage on one spreads to the others.
carmilla.analysis:
Carmilla lives in contact. Her passive makes her steal part of the defenses of the heroes she touches, her flowers revolve around her wounding, slowing down more and more and healing her, and her skill 2 accumulates speed before relaunching on a target to stun it, especially the longer the charge lasts. His ultimate curses an area: enemies who remain there are immobilized then linked, and as long as they remain close, a control suffered by one applies to the others, with part of the damage.

This mechanic makes its value very dependent on its allies: its best measured duos show gaps among the strongest recorded, with Diggie, Floryn, Mathilda and Chip. If enemies move away from each other, the bond breaks. She is among the reinforced heroes of patch 2.1.88, with no details published on the wiki. The measurements place her in difficulty against X.Borg, Valentina, Natalia and Lesley.

tigreal.summary: Historical initiator tank, capable of bringing together an entire team in a single ultimate.
tigreal.analysis:
Tigreal does one thing, and he does it better than almost anyone: pick up multiple opponents at once. The classic combo is to rush in with skill 2, then immediately chain the ultimate before the targets disperse — canceling the animation with a Flicker spell remains the most profitable technique to learn on him.

Its limit is clear: apart from its ultimate, it brings almost nothing. A Tigreal who missed his initiation leaves his team with four for around ten seconds. He's a hero of timing, not continuous presence.

franco.summary: Initiation tank whose entire part fits in a grappling hook: it removes a player from the map.
franco.analysis:
Franco does not play the same game as the other tanks. He's not looking to absorb damage, he's looking to remove an opponent from combat before it begins. A successful grapple on the opposing shooter, followed by the ultimate, is a dead player and a free objective.

Its entire value therefore rests on the precision of a slow projectile skill, which vision entirely determines. Franco plays in the bushes, not in the lane. A Franco who misses three grapples in a row is dead weight; a Franco who touches them wins the game alone.

khufra.analysis:
Khufra exists to cater to a specific category of heroes—those who are constantly on the move. Its skill 1 places a field that interrupts any dash it passes through, which neutralizes Fanny, Ling, Wanwan or Benedetta in a way that no other tank allows.

Apart from this response role, it remains an excellent initiator: the ultimate ball propels opponents and allows them to be pushed back against a turret or a wall. Its weakness is its recharge: apart from skills, Khufra is slow and easy to bypass.

belerick.summary: Taunt tank that responds to each series of blows received: the more you hit it, the more it hurts.
belerick.analysis:
Belerick is built to be hit. His passive shoots the nearest enemy as he takes damage, and increases the HP he gains from his items and emblems. Its two controls are provocations: skill 1 slows down on a line then provokes, after a short delay, the enemies remaining on the line, and the ultimate provokes everything around it. His skill 2 accelerates him, greatly slows down his target and heals him, and each trigger of the passive shortens its recharge.

Its damage depends on the damage it receives: a team that ignores it takes away most of its response, and the provocation of skill 1 gives time to leave the line. His measured win rate is highest in short games and declines slowly thereafter. The measurements place him in difficulty against Lesley, Beatrix, Brody, Natalia and Marcel.

atlas.summary: Initiator tank which attracts several heroes at once and places them wherever he decides.
atlas.analysis:
Atlas engages in two stages. His ultimate throws chains that slow down hit heroes while he channels, then, revived, pulls them towards him and crushes them in the chosen location; only a deletion can interrupt it. His skill 2 makes him come out of his armor to move faster, immune to slowdowns, before the machine joins him by stunning around it. Each skill launched creates a zone of cold around itself which slows down, then freezes the enemies who remain there.

His numbers vary depending on the rank: his measured victory rate is higher in Mythic and Mythic Honor than in Mythic Glory, where he is however more banned. He is among the reinforced heroes of patch 2.1.88, with no details published on the wiki. His best duets measured are with supports – Mathilda, Floryn, Estes, Rafaela – and the measurements place him clearly in difficulty against Marcel, then against Wanwan, Alice, Valentina and Lancelot.

He leaves the machine, faster and insensitive to slowdowns, while it follows him faster and faster. When they join together, nearby enemies are damaged and stunned. Pilot and machine share a HP bar and take less damage during this phase.

Launches chains that slow down heroes hit while channeling, which only interrupts a removal. Relaunched, it brings them back towards it and crushes them in the chosen place. Out of its armor, the machine returns immediately but the stun becomes a slowdown.
strengths: Move multiple heroes at once with ultimate
A pipeline interrupted only by a deletion
Insensitive to slowdowns when leaving the machine
A cold zone that slows down and then freezes
weaknesses: Clearly in difficulty against Marcel according to the measurements
Win rate measured lower in Mythic Glory
A stun lost if the ultimate goes out of its armor
In difficulty against Wanwan, Alice and Valentina

barats.summary: Tank jungler whose mount grows with each skill that hits, and who swallows an opponent only to spit them out against a wall.
barats.analysis:
Barats plays on accumulation. Each skill that hits makes Detona, his mount, grow bigger and gives him additional defenses; at maximum charge, its basic attacks become area tramples which maintain the effect. Skill 2 slows down and brings enemies back towards him, and the ultimate throws Detona on the first enemy hit: the target is swallowed, neutralized, then spat out, and explodes with a stun if it hits a hero or a wall. Barats is unresponsive to controls during the maneuver.

Its measured performance is concentrated at the start of the game: high victory rate in short games, then below fifty percent after the sixteenth minute. It is growing in popularity, with selection and ban rates increasing over the last thirty days. The measurements place him very clearly in difficulty facing X.Borg, then facing Gord, Alice, Yve and Uranus.
skills: Each skill that hits adds a charge for a few seconds: Detona grows and gains defenses and resistance to controls. At max charge, his basic attacks become AoE stomps that extend charges.
Detona spits oil in a fan, which Barats immediately ignites. The area grows with the number of charges: this is its ability to clean and maintain the charges.
Two missiles fall on an area and slow down, then their blast pushes enemies towards Barats. Used to bring a target within range of the ultimate.

After a short delay, Detona charges and swallows the first enemy hit, incapacitating them and then spitting them out. If the target hits a hero or a wall, it explodes and stuns nearby enemies. Barats ignores checks for the duration, and canceling refunds part of the cooldown.
strengths: Defenses that increase with each skill that hits
An ultimate that neutralizes a target and stuns against a wall
Unaffected by controls during the ultimate
A skill 2 that brings enemies towards him
weaknesses: Win rate measured as a clear drop in long games
Must touch his skills to keep his charges
Very clearly in difficulty against X.Borg according to measurements

builds.name: Jungle Tank

minotaur.summary: Roam tank who heals his team as much as he protects them, and whose ultimate makes him go into a rage to strengthen his skills.
minotaur.analysis:
Minotaur provides two things: control and healing. His skill 1 makes him jump over an area, briefly throwing enemies and reinforcing his following attacks; his skill 2 heals the most injured ally nearby as well as himself. The ultimate hits the ground three times, slows down then throws it into the air, making it insensitive to controls during the attack and causing it to go into a rage: for several seconds, its skills are reinforced and its healing affects all nearby allies.

He is rarely banned despite a victory rate measured above average at all ranks, a gap which slowly erodes in long games. He is among the reinforced heroes of patch 2.1.88, with no details published on the wiki. The measurements place him in difficulty against Beatrix, Ixia, Carmilla, Alice and Yve.
skills: Each skill launched gives him a temporary bonus and heals him for part of the damage inflicted on him by opposing heroes. In rage, these effects are doubled.
Jumps over an area, briefly throws enemies and slows them, then strengthens its basic attacks for a few seconds. In rage, area and damage increase.
Heals the most injured nearby ally and himself, based on his missing HP. In rage, the healing extends to all nearby allies: this is the skill to keep for the end of a fight.
Hit the ground three times: the first two hits slow down significantly, the last one throws into the air. He ignores controls during the attack, then rages for several seconds with enhanced skills.
strengths: A heal on the most injured ally, then on all enraged allies
Two projections, at the leap and at the ultimate
Unaffected by controls during the ultimate
Win rate measured above average at all ranks
weaknesses: Skills only strengthened during the rage following the ultimate
Measured win rate which erodes in long games
In difficulty against Beatrix, Ixia and Carmilla according to measurements
